headings.title: State payment of costs in capital and penitentiary conviction cases
headings.reviewNote: Requires state to pay costs (except costs incurred on defendant's behalf) when indigent defendant is convicted in a capital case, sentenced to penitentiary, or under 18 and jailed for a penitentiary-only offense.

headings.title: Sheriff per diem compensation for sequestered felony jury board and lodging
headings.reviewNote: Requires sheriff to furnish sequestered felony juries with board and lodging unless otherwise ordered, allowing up to $3.50 daily per juror and officer in charge taxed as costs paid by state unless recovered from convicted defendant.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and statutory history; state cost liability for indigent capital/penitentiary/under-18 convictions (excluding defense costs) and sheriff sequestered felony jury board/lodging up to $3.50/day verified.

headings.title: Cost liability between counties upon change of venue and fine allocation
headings.reviewNote: Requires originating county to pay trial and jail-confinement costs to receiving county on change of venue (except improper venue transfer) and directs criminal fines and bond forfeitures to originating county's public school fund.

headings.title: Statutory definition of costs in venue change proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'costs' for this section to include statutory civil/criminal costs, direct defendant/court/jury/witness care and security salaries, chapter 494 jury expenses, and other judge-approved necessary trial expenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections, statutory history, and 2 cross-references (545.620, 221.260); inter-county change-of-venue cost reimbursement (excluding improper-venue transfer), originating-county school fund fines, and four-part costs definition verified.

headings.title: Certification and filing of criminal court cost bills with treasurers
headings.reviewNote: Requires circuit clerks to certify criminal court cost bills to DOC director and file copies with respective county treasurers and the city of St. Louis.

headings.title: Warrants on state treasurer and reimbursement limited to county expenses
headings.reviewNote: Governs state treasurer warrants on DOC-certified bills with state-due withholding and county-only reimbursement, plus county commission and St. Louis comptroller payment warrants with fee lists.

headings.title: Treasurer record keeping in criminal cost bill account books
headings.reviewNote: Requires treasurers receiving warrants and criminal court cost bills to record them in well-bound books corresponding as near as may be to section 50.470 accounts.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 3 subsections, statutory history, and effective date 7-01-06; circuit clerk cost-bill certification and county/city treasurer copies, state-offset warrants limited to county costs, and section 50.470 account books verified.

headings.title: Definitions of department and jail reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'department' (Department of Corrections) and 'jail reimbursement' (daily state per diem for custody time) for this section.

headings.title: State per diem reimbursement up to thirty-seven dollars and fifty cents
headings.reviewNote: Directs DOC, subject to appropriation and review, to reimburse counties and cities not within a county up to $37.50 per offender per day for four listed correctional commitment/detention categories.

headings.title: Sheriff certification of custody days and two-year claim submission window
headings.reviewNote: Requires sheriff or city chief executive officer to certify custody days when state is liable for costs and permits submitting claims within two years of eligibility.

headings.title: Department eligibility determination, rulemaking authority, and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs DOC eligibility review, payment remittance, and chapter 536/section 536.028 rulemaking, with nonseverability voiding post-August 28, 2025 rules if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 4 subsections and statutory history (L. 2025 H.B. 199); definitions, $37.50/day appropriation-subject DOC jail reimbursement criteria, sheriff 2-year claim submission, and chapter 536 rulemaking with August 28, 2025 nonseverability verified.
